title: A Statistical Benchmark for Diffusion-Posterior-Sampling Algorithms
claim: Reverse-diffusion trajectories commit to sparse, jump-like structure only at late diffusion times, and the extent of this depends on the prior.
layout: 4x4 grid of line plots; rows are priors, columns are diffusion times, left to right
description: A 4x4 grid of small line plots. Each row is a prior (BL(0.1,1), St(1), Laplace(1), Gauss(0.1,1)), labeled on the left. Each column is a diffusion time (t=999, 600, 200, 0), labeled on top. Every panel shows three sampled 1-D signals of length 64 as blue, red and green lines with different markers. At t=999 the signals look like noisy white noise and are almost identical across rows. Moving right, they become smoother and more structured. For BL at t=0 they turn into piecewise-constant staircases with large jumps. For St they show heavy-tailed jumps, with y-axis scales reaching 50 or more. For Laplace and Gauss they look like rough random walks. The eye goes first to the right-hand column, where the differences between priors are clearest.
caption: Unconditional reverse-diffusion trajectories obtained by \glsxtrshort{ddpm} sampling with the oracle denoiser. Rows: Jump distributions. Columns: Diffusion times. Line styles: Different initializations and random states.
abstract: We propose a statistical benchmark for diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) algorithms for Bayesian linear inverse problems. The benchmark synthesizes signals from sparse LÃ©vy-process priors whose posteriors admit efficient Gibbs methods. These Gibbs methods can be used to obtain gold-standard posterior samples that can be compared to the samples obtained by the DPS algorithms. By using the Gibbs methods for the resolution of the denoising problems in the reverse diffusion, the framework also isolates the error that arises from the approximations to the likelihood score. We instantiate the benchmark with the minimum-mean-squared-error optimality gap and posterior coverage tests and provide numerical experiments for popular DPS algorithms on the inverse problems of denoising, deconvolution, imputation, and reconstruction from partial Fourier measurements. We release the benchmark code at https://github.com/zacmar/dps-benchmark. The repository exposes simple plug-in interfaces, reference scripts, and config-driven runs so that new algorithms can be added and evaluated with minimal effort. We invite researchers to contribute and report results.
